name: Hydrolytic Dispersion Charge HDC-2 'Saltflat'
description: The HDC-2 is a two-stage chemical-explosive device designed for data infrastructure denial. The outer shell contains a conventional shaped charge that ruptures a pressurized inner reservoir filled with a superheated hydrolytic solution — a proprietary TESSERA CORPONATION compound that aggressively attacks organic polymers, fiber-optic cladding, and unshielded circuit substrates on contact. The blast itself is modest; the real damage is the dispersed chemical payload that coats surfaces in a 5-meter radius with a compound that continues reacting for up to 40 minutes after detonation.
specifications:
weight: 1.2 kg
dimensions: 14 cm x 8 cm cylindrical
blast radius: 5 m primary, 9 m chemical drift
chemical active duration: 35–45 minutes post-detonation
trigger modes: Remote detonation, Timer, Tamper-triggered
neutralization agent: TESSERA proprietary NeutraFlush compound (sold separately)
casing material: Corrosion-resistant ceramic-alloy shell
tactical_use: Deployed in corporate sabotage operations targeting server farms, communication hubs, and fabrication lines. Teams plant HDC-2 units inside conduit junctions or cable management systems where the chemical dispersal maximizes contact with sensitive infrastructure. Anti-personnel use is considered secondary — the hydrolytic compound causes severe chemical burns, but the weapon is rarely chosen for its human lethality. It is exceptionally effective at making a location digitally dead for hours.
cultural_context: The HDC-2 is the calling card of data-warfare crews and anti-corporate saboteurs in Meridian 88. Finding one at a crime scene tells investigators less about who planted it and more about what the target was — if someone used a Saltflat, they wanted the data gone more than they wanted people dead. TESSERA markets a civilian variant for 'industrial equipment decommissioning,' which fools no one.
known_users: Insurance fraud operators targeting competitor facilities
story_hooks: A runner is hired to plant an HDC-2 in a competitor's server room, only to find the room already destroyed by an identical charge — someone got there first, and the data the runner was supposed to destroy is already gone.

A TESSERA 'decommissioning' team is found dead in an industrial district, their own HDC-2 units detonated around them. The chemical burns suggest the charges were triggered remotely — from inside TESSERA's own network.
The NeutraFlush neutralization compound has been pulled from the market without explanation, and three active HDC-2 sites in the city are now impossible to safely contain.
